headline: Models steering generative design of antimicrobial peptides and drug-like small molecules
label: Generative Ml Antimicrobial Design
summary: Target-conditioned generative models now pair with property predictors to design candidates against specific pathogens and structural constraints.
synthesis: The common thread is predictive modelling embedded in the design loop for antimicrobial and peptide-based candidates, rather than post hoc analysis of existing compounds. A conditional VAE combined with conditional diffusion generates pathogen-targeted antimicrobial peptides with programmable physicochemical properties, with MIC predictors in the loop. A 33-model ensemble builds a five-axis drug-likeness profile to rank 16M molecules, and a lead antibacterial compound is reported as validated. EDWARD generates small molecules from peptide-protein complexes via fragment and scaffold assembly under E(3)-equivariant pharmacophore constraints. HELM-BERT, a DeBERTa-based encoder pretrained on HELM notation for 39,079 peptides, outperforms SMILES language models on cyclic peptide permeability. What is new is explicit target conditioning, whether pathogen specificity, drug-likeness axes, or structural pharmacophore constraints, coupled to generative or large-scale design.
